get.description:
**Allowed Scopes**: _`settlement:read`_

Returns settlements. For more information about settlements, see [this guide](/reference/how-to-use-spend-data). Settlements data are cached for up to 24 hours. A successful `PUT /v1/settlements/state` clears the cached settlement reads, so the next call is fresh; state changes from accounting exports or made in Spendesk can take up to 24 hours to appear.

This endpoint uses page-based pagination. Use `page` and `pageSize` to retrieve additional results. The maximum `pageSize` is 30. Continue fetching while `page * pageSize < meta.pagination.total`.

To filter by settlement status, use `state` (for example, `/v1/settlements?page=1&pageSize=30&state=created`).

Settlements expose allocation links through `allocations[].payableId`. For accounting export use cases that require payable line amounts, retrieve the related payable and read `lineItems[].financial.netAmount`. Amounts are expressed in the smallest unit of the currency.

post.description:
**Allowed Scopes**: _`payable:read`_

Request an extract (snapshot) of expenses to be created.

A request to create a snapshot of expenses according to the filters provided will be queued, where a key (of format UUID) will be returned immediately, it being a reference to your request.

This key can be used to check for the status of this request using the [GET Snapshot Payable](/reference/v1-get-snapshot-payables) API call. Once its status is "COMPLETE", the list of payables is returned under the "result.data" element of the response.

Requesting snapshots should be done sequentially and cannot be done simultaneously (in parallel). Requesting a new snapshot with exactly the same parameters will return the same key as long as the snapshot exists. Snapshots are typically cached for 10 hours.

These two APIs ([POST](/reference/v1-create-snapshot-payables) and [GET](/reference/v1-get-snapshot-payables)) are implemented based on the [asynchronous request-response pattern](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/async-request-reply), decoupling long-running backend jobs from the synchronous nature of REST APIs.

For more information about payables, see this [guide](/reference/how-to-use-spend-data).

get.description:
**Allowed Scopes**: _`payable:read`_

Returns an extract (snapshot) of payables requested via the [POST API](/reference/v1-create-snapshot-payables). Requires the returned key as a parameter.

Due to its asynchronous nature, we recommend to poll this endpoint ideally after 1 hour, or alternatively every 5 minutes until status is "COMPLETE" or "ERROR".

The list of expenses is returned under "result.data" when its status is "COMPLETE". The response is paginated (30 payables per page), where the current page number is returned under "result.meta.pagination". Snapshots are typically cached for 10 hours.

These two APIs ([POST](/reference/v1-create-snapshot-payables) and [GET](/reference/v1-get-snapshot-payables)) are implemented based on the [asynchronous request-response pattern](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/async-request-reply), decoupling long-running backend jobs from the synchronous nature of REST APIs.

For more information about payables, see this [guide](/reference/how-to-use-spend-data).

searchPayablePaymentStatusFilter.description: Filter payables by payment status. `toPay` means any outstanding balance remains — it INCLUDES partially-paid invoices and does NOT mean 'fully unpaid'. `paid` means the allocations on the payable sum to its full amount, leaving zero outstanding (settlements and/or credit notes, so a credit note alone can make an invoice `paid`); it EXCLUDES partially-paid invoices, which are classified as `toPay`. Payment status is not returned on the payable, and the amount fields are always the full invoice value, never reduced by partial payments. So: to size true outstanding AP, sum `outstandingFunctionalAmount` (the authoritative server-computed remainder, in the company's functional currency; `outstandingAmount` is the same figure in each payable's own currency and is therefore NOT summable across currencies) rather than summing `amount` over `toPay` payables, and fall back to `amount` minus `allocations[]` only on payables where those fields are absent. To size total cash paid out, use get_settlements rather than summing `amount` over `paid` payables (which omits the partial payments already made on still-open `toPay` invoices) — do NOT aggregate `allocations[]` for cash: only `entityType: 'settlement'` entries are money moved, while `reversal` (on an expense) and `expense` (on a credit note) entries are credit notes or card refunds applied document-to-document, so an invoice fully covered by a credit note reports `paid` with `outstandingAmount` 0 and zero cash paid; allocation amounts also carry the sign of the payable they sit on, so allocations on credit-note payables are negative.
searchPayablePaymentStatusFilter.title: searchPayablePaymentStatusFilter

searchPayableStringFieldFilter.description: Filter payables by a string field (description or documentaryEvidenceNumber).
searchPayableStringFieldFilter.title: searchPayableStringFieldFilter

searchPayableAmountFieldFilter.description: Filter payables by an amount field. `grossAmount` is the payable's total. `netAmount` and `vatAmount` are not totals: each item line is tested on its own and a payable matches when ANY one line meets the condition (so `netAmount > 5000` misses a payable with two 3,000 lines, and payables with no item lines never match); for a threshold on a payable's net or VAT total, sum itemLines[].netAmount / vatAmount client-side (they are in the payable's own currency, not the functional currency). `value` is a DECIMAL amount in MAJOR units of the company's functional currency (the currency of functionalAmount), NOT the minor-unit coefficient returned in money objects and NOT the payable's own currency: for payables over EUR 5,000.00 use `{ "field": "grossAmount", "operator": ">", "value": 5000 }`, not 500000.
searchPayableAmountFieldFilter.title: searchPayableAmountFieldFilter

searchPayableDateFieldFilter.description: Filter payables by a date field (payableDate, firstCreatedAt, firstExportedAt, lastUpdatedAt, dueDate, accountingDate).
searchPayableDateFieldFilter.title: searchPayableDateFieldFilter

searchPayableBooleanFieldFilter.description: Filter payables by the withBookkeepingStartDate boolean. When true, excludes payables dated before the company's bookkeeping start date (the onboarding/migration cutover), keeping only those whose creationDate is on or after it — or all payables when the company has no start date configured. When false, the filter is a no-op and returns everything.

get.description:
Start the PKCE authorization-code flow for an OAuth app.

Use this endpoint only for OAuth app credentials that require a Spendesk user to authorize access. Do not use it with Public API credentials; server-to-server Public API credentials should request a bearer token from [Create Access Token](/reference/v1-create-auth-token).

parameters.name: response_type
parameters.description: Always `code`.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: OAuth app `client_id` provided by Spendesk.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: URI to redirect the user after connection is authorized. If successful, the redirect URL will look like: `{redirect_uri}?code={auth_code}&state={state}&iss={issuer}`, where `iss` is the authorization server issuer (RFC 9207), `code` is the `authorization` code to be used in the [Request Access Token endpoint](/public/reference/v1-create-oauth2-token), and `state` allows you to verify the integrity of the connection.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description:
Optional field to restrict the scope of the token. The default scope will match the scope defined in the front end when generating your API client id and secret.

See [available scopes](/reference/scopes) for more information.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: This string will be sent back at the end of the OAuth2 flow, so that whoever starts the flow can double-check that the same variable is being returned (and there has been no tampering).

parameters.name: code_challenge
parameters.description: The client should locally generate a `secret` (AKA `code_verifier`), that at this initial stage of the OAuth2 flow should be passed as a `code_challenge` in the format of `base64url(sha256(secret))`. You can find an example about that [here](https://www.oauth.com/playground/authorization-code-with-pkce.html).

parameters.name: code_challenge_method
parameters.description: Always `S256`.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: Optional RFC 8707 resource indicator. Ignored for standard OAuth clients — any value (including an empty string) is accepted and never read. For public MCP dynamic client registration clients it is required and must match the MCP resource URL; that check is enforced in business logic once the client is resolved.

302.description: On success: redirect to the Spendesk consent page `{spendesk_frontend}?id={token_id}&code={consent_handle}`; `consent_handle` is not an authorization code and cannot be exchanged for tokens. On a validated-client error: redirect to `{redirect_uri}?error={code}&error_description={msg}&state={state}&iss={issuer}` (RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1, RFC 9207). On an unverifiable client or redirect_uri: redirect to the Spendesk error page `/auth/oauth2/error?error={code}`.

post.description:
Standard OAuth2 token endpoint for OAuth app credentials. Use `grant_type=authorization_code` to exchange an authorization code for access and refresh tokens after [Request Authorization](/reference/v1-request-authorization). Use `grant_type=refresh_token` on this same endpoint to rotate tokens and keep the connection alive.

OAuth token requests should be sent as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, as specified by OAuth 2.0. JSON requests remain accepted for backwards compatibility.

Do not use this endpoint with Public API credentials issued for server-to-server access. Those credentials must call [Create Access Token](/reference/v1-create-auth-token) on `/v1/auth/token`.

The legacy [Refresh token endpoint](/reference/v1-refresh-oauth2-token) remains available temporarily for backwards compatibility.

If a refresh fails:
- 401 "Provided secret does not match the client", "client_secret is required for this client" or "The requested token does not belong to the provided client": the `client_id`/`client_secret` you sent are wrong (for example another environment's app). Fix them and retry with the same refresh token, which was not consumed.
- 401 "No active OAuth2 client found for provided credentials": the client is unknown, disabled or expired. Check `client_id`, or register or re-enable the client; retrying with the same credentials will not help. The refresh token was not consumed, but it only works with the client it was issued to.
- Any other 401, and a 403: this refresh token can no longer be used (expired, revoked or already rotated). Discard it and ask the user to reconnect.
- 400: the request is malformed. 5xx: temporary, retry later with the same refresh token.

Bulk syncs (creates or upserts) accounts for the selected account type. Each item replaces the stored account: an omitted description, code, creditCode, auxiliaryCode, externalId, purpose, taxRate or currency is cleared to null (an omitted externalId removes the ERP link). An item without id that has a code and does not set isArchived to true updates the non-archived account of the same type with the same code, purpose, auxiliaryCode and taxRate (for reverseCharge: the same name, code and creditCode), if there is one. Items without id never match an archived account. For partial updates to existing accounts, use PATCH /v1/experimental/accounts.

get.description:
**Allowed Scopes**: _`experimental:external-reference:read`_

  Returns the IDs Spendesk entities have in an external system (ERP), as one entry per
  (entity, external ID) pair. Filter by `entityIds` to get the external IDs of entities you
  already know, or by `externalIds` to resolve external IDs back to Spendesk entities — at
  least one of the two is required.

  Where the reference is stored is an implementation detail. Reference entities (`supplier`,
  `employee`, `analyticalField`, `analyticalFieldValue`, `costCenter`, `expenseCategory`,
  `customField`) are served from the entity registry; exportable entities (`payable`,
  `settlementAllocation`, `walletLoad`, `bankFee`, `documentaryEvidenceAttachment`,
  `creditNoteAllocation`) from the export state, where only exported entities carry an external
  ID; and the account kinds from the chart of accounts.

  The chart of accounts is addressed one account type at a time — `bankAccount`,
  `expenseAccount`, `taxAccount`, `supplierAccount`, `employeeAccount` or
  `reverseChargeAccount` — each returning only accounts of that type. An account's type is
  part of what identifies it, so there is no unqualified spelling. The suffix is required
  because `supplier` and `employee` already name reference entities. For these, `entityId` is the
  account id and `externalName` is the account name; archived accounts and accounts without an
  external ID are never returned, and `provider` and `source` are always null because an
  account row records no provenance — so filtering by either returns no accounts.

  `source` tells you who recorded the mapping: `native_integration` means a native ERP sync
  owns it and keeps it up to date, `public_api` means it was set through this API.

  Cached for up to 24 hours. Changes made through the API are returned by subsequent reads; changes made in Spendesk can take up to 24 hours to appear.

parameters.name: entityType
parameters.description: Kind of Spendesk entity. Reference entities: `supplier`, `employee`, `analyticalField`, `analyticalFieldValue`, `costCenter`, `expenseCategory`, `customField`. Chart of accounts, one account type at a time: `bankAccount`, `expenseAccount`, `taxAccount`, `supplierAccount`, `employeeAccount`, `reverseChargeAccount` — each also asserts the target account's own type. Exportable entities: `payable`, `settlementAllocation`, `walletLoad`, `bankFee`, `documentaryEvidenceAttachment`, `creditNoteAllocation`.

parameters.name: entityIds
parameters.description: Filter by Spendesk entity ids (comma-separated).

parameters.name: externalIds
parameters.description: Filter by external ids (comma-separated).

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Filter by external system.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Filter by who recorded the mapping.

parameters.name: first

post.description:
**Allowed Scopes**: _`experimental:external-reference:write`_

  Records the ID a Spendesk entity has in an external system (ERP), namespaced by `provider`.
  Re-sending the same `(entityType, provider, externalId)` updates the existing record.

  **Recording an external ID for an exportable entity** (payable, settlementAllocation,
  walletLoad, bankFee, documentaryEvidenceAttachment, creditNoteAllocation) **also records that
  entity as exported** to the given provider, and it will then appear under
  `GET /v1/experimental/integrations/export-status?status=exported`. Use it when you have
  genuinely exported the entity to your own system. For reference entities (`supplier`,
  `employee`, `analyticalField`, `analyticalFieldValue`, `costCenter`, `expenseCategory`,
  `customField`) the write only stores the mapping and has no export side effect.

  **For the account kinds** the external ID is set on the account itself, so `entityId` is the
  account id — never the id of the supplier or employee an account of that type points at — and
  `provider`, `externalName` and `componentId` are ignored, since an account row has nowhere
  to keep them. `provider` is still required because the other kinds need it; send any non-empty
  value. The account kinds are `bankAccount`, `expenseAccount`, `taxAccount`,
  `supplierAccount`, `employeeAccount` and `reverseChargeAccount`; each asserts the target
  account's own type, and the write is refused if it disagrees rather than applied to the wrong
  account. There is no unqualified spelling, since an account's type is part of what identifies
  it. An external ID must identify a
  single account, so a write is also refused when another active account of the same type and
  purpose already holds the value, and when a second reference in the same request gives one
  account a different external ID.

  Companies whose ERP is connected through a **native** integration cannot set external IDs at all:
  Spendesk talks to that ERP directly and owns the mappings end to end. For accounts that is what
  keeps the chart of accounts safe — it is synced from the ERP, and `externalId` is the ERP's own
  key, so an API value there would be overwritten by the next sync.

  Two exportable cases behave differently. While a **native** integration is mid-export for the
  entity the write is refused: that integration owns the export it is running and records its own
  external ID when the ERP answers. While a **file-based** export is mid-flight the external ID is
  stored but the export state is left untouched, since that export is not ours to complete.

  A native integration always takes precedence, and an API write never overwrites a value it owns.
  For a reference entity the write is refused when a native sync already records an external ID for
  that entity under the same `provider`, or when the external ID itself already belongs to a
  natively synced entity — a different `provider` is still accepted, since references are
  namespaced per ERP. For an exportable entity the write is refused whenever a native external ID
  is already recorded, whatever `provider` you send, because there is a single external ID per
  entity and component. Values you recorded through this API can be corrected freely.

  Purchase orders are not accepted: `externalPONumber` is set on the purchase order itself at
  creation time, so a second copy here would compete with it.

  Each reference gets its own `outcome`, in request order — `exported` when the entity is now
  recorded as exported, `recorded` when the external ID was stored but the export state was left
  alone, `mapped` for a reference-entity or account write, and `failed` with a `reason`
  otherwise. A batch may
  mix entity kinds, so it can partially succeed: check every entry rather than the status code alone.

entityType.description: Kind of Spendesk entity. Reference entities: `supplier`, `employee`, `analyticalField`, `analyticalFieldValue`, `costCenter`, `expenseCategory`, `customField`. Chart of accounts, one account type at a time: `bankAccount`, `expenseAccount`, `taxAccount`, `supplierAccount`, `employeeAccount`, `reverseChargeAccount` — each also asserts the target account's own type. Exportable entities: `payable`, `settlementAllocation`, `walletLoad`, `bankFee`, `documentaryEvidenceAttachment`, `creditNoteAllocation`.

**Allowed Scopes**: _`experimental:chart-of-accounts:write`_

Triggers a refresh of the company's accounting integration settings, pulling accounts, tax accounts, analytical fields, suppliers, employees and currencies from the connected accounting software.

The refresh runs asynchronously: a 202 means it was accepted, not that the refreshed data is available yet. Refreshes are throttled per company, so a second call made shortly after a successful one returns 429 with a `Retry-After` header. Accounting integrations that have no settings synchronisation return 409.

**Allowed Scopes**: _`supplier:read`_

Returns suppliers existing in the Spendesk entity (company). Supplier data is cached for up to 24 hours; supplier account data (used for `accountPayable`) is cached for up to 20 minutes. Changes made through the API are returned by subsequent reads; changes made in Spendesk can take up to 24 hours to appear.

Pass `include=externalIds` to embed the IDs each supplier has in external systems (ERPs). It is opt-in because it costs one additional lookup per request.

invoiceId.description: Opaque unique identifier of an invoice.
invoiceId.title: invoiceId

invoiceType.description:
Kind of document the record represents. 

| Type | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `invoice` | A supplier invoice: an amount the company owes the supplier for goods or services. Amounts are positive. |
| `creditNote` | A supplier credit note: a document from the same supplier that reduces an amount owed (a refund, cancellation, or correction of a prior invoice). Amounts are negative. |
invoiceType.title: invoiceType

invoiceStage.description:
Where the invoice or credit note is in its lifecycle; exactly one value at a time. `paymentStatus` and `exportStatus` move in parallel. 

| Stage | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `pendingApproval` | Awaiting a decision in the approval workflow. |
| `inReview` | Approved, waiting for the controller review. |
| `disputed` | Approved, then put in dispute with the supplier. Invoices only. |
| `toSettle` | Reviewed. An invoice is waiting for payment, fully or in part (`paymentStatus` tells which); a credit note is partially allocated. |
| `settled` | An invoice is fully paid; a credit note is fully allocated or reimbursed. |
| `rejected` | Declined by an approver, rejected in controller review, or expired. |
| `cancelled` | Withdrawn by the company: archived after a supplier dispute, or replaced by a corrective invoice. Invoices withdrawn by their submitter are never returned. |
invoiceStage.title: invoiceStage

paymentStatus.description:
Settlement state, independent of where the money moved (Spendesk or elsewhere) and of `stage`. On a single invoice with `payments`, it is aggregated over settled (`paid`) payments in the invoice `currency` only; on the invoice list, on credit notes (which have no stored payment status, so always report `unpaid`), and when `payments` is empty, it is the stored payment status instead, so the list and the single invoice can disagree and the `amountPaid` conditions below hold only for the aggregated case. Scheduling and per-transfer failures are visible on individual payments, not here. 

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `unpaid` | Nothing has settled (`amountPaid` equals 0). |
| `partiallyPaid` | Some but not all has settled (`0 < amountPaid < grossAmount`). |
| `paid` | Fully settled (`amountDue` equals 0), by any means. |

A `returned` payment reduces `amountPaid`, so this can move back from `paid` to `partiallyPaid` or `unpaid`.
paymentStatus.title: paymentStatus

exportStatus.description:
Accounting-export state — whether the invoice has been exported to the customer's accounting system or ERP. Independent of `stage` and `paymentStatus`. The ledger posting date is `accountingDate`; the export timestamp is `exportedAt`. Only meaningful once the invoice has an accounting payable — the invoice's `exportStatus` field itself is null for invoices that don't have one yet. 

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `pending` | Not yet exported. |
| `exported` | Successfully exported to the accounting system. |
| `failed` | An export attempt failed and needs attention. |
exportStatus.title: exportStatus

documentaryEvidenceStatus.description:
Status of the supporting document — the supplier's invoice or credit-note file — that justifies the payable for audit and tax purposes. Only meaningful once the invoice has an accounting payable — the invoice's `documentaryEvidenceStatus` field itself is null for invoices that don't have one yet. 

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `provided` | A document is attached. |
| `missing` | No document is attached yet. |
| `cannotBeProvided` | The buyer declared that no document can be provided; a signed affidavit stands in its place. |
| `declaredAsInvalid` | An attached document was reviewed and marked invalid (e.g. wrong file or unreadable). |

Certification/compliance details (e.g. the Spanish "Digitised Paper Receipt") are intentionally out of scope of this field and will be exposed via a dedicated compliance field once its format is finalised.
documentaryEvidenceStatus.title: documentaryEvidenceStatus

paymentSource.description:
Who executed the payment. 

| Source | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `spendesk` | Orchestrated and executed through Spendesk (scheduled, confirmed, transferred). |
| `external` | Happened outside Spendesk (own bank, cash, another tool) and is recorded here for reporting/bookkeeping. External payments have no Spendesk orchestration. |
paymentSource.title: paymentSource

paymentMethod.description: Means of payment. Extensible — new methods may be added over time, so treat unknown values defensively. `other` is a catch-all.
paymentMethod.title: paymentMethod

supplierRef.description: Reference to the supplier (counterparty) of the invoice.

id.description: Supplier id. Fetch full supplier details from `GET /v1/suppliers/{id}`.

supplierRef.title: supplierRef

purchaseOrderRef.description: Reference to a purchase order the invoice is matched against (two/three-way match).
purchaseOrderRef.title: purchaseOrderRef

costCenterRef.description: Reference to a cost center (the internal unit that bears the cost).

id.description: Cost-center id. Use `GET /v1/cost-centers` to resolve full details.

costCenterRef.title: costCenterRef

expenseCategoryRef.description: Reference to an expense category — the customer's spend taxonomy (e.g. Software, Travel, Meals) used for accounting and analytics. Distinct from the cost center (which bears the cost) and from analytical fields (free custom dimensions).

id.description: Expense-category id. Use `GET /v1/expense-categories` to resolve full details.

expenseCategoryRef.title: expenseCategoryRef

analyticalProperty.description: A value set for one analytical field. Analytical fields are the customer's own bookkeeping dimensions (custom fields) — e.g. project, team — used to classify and report spend. `valueId`/`valueName` are null when the field applies but no value is selected.
analyticalProperty.title: analyticalProperty

invoiceAnalyticalSplit.description: One allocation of the whole invoice to a cost center and/or analytical-field values, as a share of its total. Splits apply to the invoice as a whole, not to individual line items.

costCenter.description: Cost center this share is allocated to, or null when the split only sets analytical-field values.

percentage.description: Percentage of the invoice allocated to this split, from 0 to 100 (e.g. `25` means 25%). The splits of an invoice add up to 100.

analyticalProperties.description: Analytical-field values set on this split.

invoiceAnalyticalSplit.title: invoiceAnalyticalSplit

invoiceDispute.description: Details of a dispute on the invoice (contested amount, duplicate, goods/services not received, quality issue…), overlaying whatever approval/payment state the invoice holds. Not populated yet: the invoice `dispute` field is always null for now, even on an invoice in dispute with the supplier (which reports `stage` `disputed`).

reasonCode.description: Machine-readable reason the invoice is disputed (e.g. a standard dispute-reason code). Not enumerated — treat as an opaque, extensible code. Null when only a free-text reason exists.

reason.description: Human-readable reason/comment for the dispute, if recorded.

invoiceDispute.title: invoiceDispute

hasNextPage.description: Whether more results exist after this page. Convenience for `nextCursor != null`.

nextCursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or null when there are no more results.

nextUrl.description: Ready-to-follow URL for the next page (same filters + `cursor`), or null.

invoicesMeta.description: Meta object describing the invoice list pagination.
invoicesMeta.title: invoicesMeta

invoiceSummary.description: Compact representation of an invoice, returned by the list endpoint.

invoiceNumber.description: Supplier's invoice/credit-note number. Null if not captured.

dispute.description: Not populated yet: always null, even on a disputed invoice.

purchaseOrders.description: Purchase orders this invoice is matched against. Empty when the invoice references no PO.

costCenter.description: Cost center the invoice is coded to, or null when none is set. Set independently of `analyticalSplits`: the two are not reconciled and can disagree.

analyticalSplits.description: Allocation of the invoice total across cost centers and analytical-field values. Empty when the invoice is not split. Set independently of `costCenter`, so a split can name a different cost center.

expenseCategories.description: Expense categories the invoice is coded to, sorted by name. Empty when none is set. A split invoice can carry several, one per split. These ids are the ones the `expenseCategoryId` filter matches. Only the company's current expense-category field counts: if it is changed or removed, past invoices follow the new setting. A deleted category still shows on the invoices coded to it.

netAmount.description: Total before tax, in `currency`'s smallest unit. Can be null in any state, not only draft/incomplete: always for credit notes, and for older invoices whose net amount was never recorded.

taxAmount.description: Total tax, in `currency`'s smallest unit. Null whenever `netAmount` or `grossAmount` is null, so in any state for credit notes and older invoices with no recorded net amount.

grossAmount.description: Total amount including tax (`netAmount` + `taxAmount`), in `currency`'s smallest unit. Positive for invoices (owed to the supplier); negative for credit notes (owed to the company). Null when the invoice has no gross amount yet (draft/incomplete).

amountDue.description: Placeholder on this list endpoint, not the actual outstanding balance: it is derived from `paymentStatus` only, 0 when `paid`, otherwise the full `grossAmount`, so a `partiallyPaid` invoice reports its whole gross. Never treat or sum it as the outstanding balance. Null when `grossAmount` is not known yet (draft/incomplete).

issueDate.description: Date the supplier issued the invoice, as printed on the document (emission date).

dueDate.description: Date by which the invoice must be paid, per the supplier's payment terms. Null when no due date is known.

createdAt.description: When the invoice record was created in Spendesk (ingest/submission time, not the issue date).

updatedAt.description: When any field on the invoice record last changed.

get.description:
**Allowed Scopes**: _`experimental:invoice:read`_

Returns supplier invoices for the company, most-recent first by default, using forward-only cursor pagination. The `createdAfter`, `createdBefore`, `updatedAfter` and `updatedBefore` filters use only the UTC date of the value: After includes that day, Before excludes it. Invoice data is cached for up to 20 minutes. Changes, including those made through the API, can take up to 20 minutes to appear.

parameters.name: invoiceNumber
parameters.description: Filter by the supplier's invoice number (case-insensitive exact match). Ignored with type=creditNote; use search to find a credit note by its number.

parameters.name: expenseCategoryId
parameters.description: Filter by expense category, matching the ids in the invoice `expenseCategories`. A split invoice matches if any of its categories does.

parameters.name: stage
parameters.description: Filter by stage; any of the listed values matches. When omitted, every stage except `cancelled` is returned; pass `cancelled` to get cancelled invoices. Draft and incomplete invoices are never listed here, not even under `pendingApproval`; fetch one by ID instead, which fails while it still lacks a supplier, issue date or currency. A credit note in dispute with the supplier is never returned or counted, under any stage.

parameters.name: paymentSource
parameters.description: Not applied yet: results are not filtered by payment source.

parameters.name: paymentMethod
parameters.description: Not applied yet: results are not filtered by payment method.

parameters.name: isDisputed
parameters.description: `true`: only invoices currently in dispute with the supplier, the same as `stage` `disputed`; `false`: all others. Combined with `stage`, both must match. An invoice archived after a dispute is `cancelled`, not disputed, and credit notes are never returned as disputed.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of invoices to return in one page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned as `meta.pagination.nextCursor` by a previous call. Omit to fetch the first page.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description: Field to sort by. Combined with `sort` to set direction.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort direction.

parameters.description: Company ID.

enum: Sorry, something has gone wrong at our end. If this persists please contact support.

invoiceId.description: Opaque unique identifier of an invoice.
invoiceId.title: invoiceId

taxRate.description: Tax rate as a percentage — e.g. `20` means 20%, `5.5` means 5.5%. Null when no rate applies or it is unknown.
taxRate.title: taxRate

invoiceType.description:
Kind of document the record represents. 

| Type | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `invoice` | A supplier invoice: an amount the company owes the supplier for goods or services. Amounts are positive. |
| `creditNote` | A supplier credit note: a document from the same supplier that reduces an amount owed (a refund, cancellation, or correction of a prior invoice). Amounts are negative. |
invoiceType.title: invoiceType

invoiceStage.description:
Where the invoice or credit note is in its lifecycle; exactly one value at a time. `paymentStatus` and `exportStatus` move in parallel. 

| Stage | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `pendingApproval` | Awaiting a decision in the approval workflow. |
| `inReview` | Approved, waiting for the controller review. |
| `disputed` | Approved, then put in dispute with the supplier. Invoices only. |
| `toSettle` | Reviewed. An invoice is waiting for payment, fully or in part (`paymentStatus` tells which); a credit note is partially allocated. |
| `settled` | An invoice is fully paid; a credit note is fully allocated or reimbursed. |
| `rejected` | Declined by an approver, rejected in controller review, or expired. |
| `cancelled` | Withdrawn by the company: archived after a supplier dispute, or replaced by a corrective invoice. Invoices withdrawn by their submitter are never returned. |
invoiceStage.title: invoiceStage

paymentStatus.description:
Settlement state, independent of where the money moved (Spendesk or elsewhere) and of `stage`. On a single invoice with `payments`, it is aggregated over settled (`paid`) payments in the invoice `currency` only; on the invoice list, on credit notes (which have no stored payment status, so always report `unpaid`), and when `payments` is empty, it is the stored payment status instead, so the list and the single invoice can disagree and the `amountPaid` conditions below hold only for the aggregated case. Scheduling and per-transfer failures are visible on individual payments, not here. 

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `unpaid` | Nothing has settled (`amountPaid` equals 0). |
| `partiallyPaid` | Some but not all has settled (`0 < amountPaid < grossAmount`). |
| `paid` | Fully settled (`amountDue` equals 0), by any means. |

A `returned` payment reduces `amountPaid`, so this can move back from `paid` to `partiallyPaid` or `unpaid`.
paymentStatus.title: paymentStatus

exportStatus.description:
Accounting-export state — whether the invoice has been exported to the customer's accounting system or ERP. Independent of `stage` and `paymentStatus`. The ledger posting date is `accountingDate`; the export timestamp is `exportedAt`. Only meaningful once the invoice has an accounting payable — the invoice's `exportStatus` field itself is null for invoices that don't have one yet. 

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `pending` | Not yet exported. |
| `exported` | Successfully exported to the accounting system. |
| `failed` | An export attempt failed and needs attention. |
exportStatus.title: exportStatus

documentaryEvidenceStatus.description:
Status of the supporting document — the supplier's invoice or credit-note file — that justifies the payable for audit and tax purposes. Only meaningful once the invoice has an accounting payable — the invoice's `documentaryEvidenceStatus` field itself is null for invoices that don't have one yet. 

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `provided` | A document is attached. |
| `missing` | No document is attached yet. |
| `cannotBeProvided` | The buyer declared that no document can be provided; a signed affidavit stands in its place. |
| `declaredAsInvalid` | An attached document was reviewed and marked invalid (e.g. wrong file or unreadable). |

Certification/compliance details (e.g. the Spanish "Digitised Paper Receipt") are intentionally out of scope of this field and will be exposed via a dedicated compliance field once its format is finalised.
documentaryEvidenceStatus.title: documentaryEvidenceStatus

paymentState.description:
State of a single payment (see `paymentStatus` for the invoice-level settlement aggregate). Spendesk-executed payments (`source: spendesk`) traverse the full lifecycle; externally-recorded payments (`source: external`) are typically created directly as `paid`. 

| State | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `scheduled` | Planned for a date but not yet confirmed; no money has moved (Spendesk only). |
| `confirmed` | Approved for release by the account owner via Strong Customer Authentication (SCA); the transfer is mandated and will be executed on the scheduled date (Spendesk only). |
| `executing` | The transfer has been sent and is in flight at the bank (Spendesk only). |
| `paid` | Executed and settled. Not necessarily terminal — a settled payment can later become `returned`. |
| `failed` | The transfer was rejected or failed before settling; see `statusReason`. A retry is a new payment entry (Spendesk only). |
| `cancelled` | A scheduled payment was cancelled before execution; no money moved. |
| `returned` | The payment had settled but the funds were later returned/clawed back by the bank (e.g. an ACH return or recall); see `statusReason`. Its amount is removed from the invoice's `amountPaid`. |
paymentState.title: paymentState

paymentSource.description:
Who executed the payment. 

| Source | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `spendesk` | Orchestrated and executed through Spendesk (scheduled, confirmed, transferred). |
| `external` | Happened outside Spendesk (own bank, cash, another tool) and is recorded here for reporting/bookkeeping. External payments have no Spendesk orchestration. |
paymentSource.title: paymentSource

paymentMethod.description: Means of payment. Extensible — new methods may be added over time, so treat unknown values defensively. `other` is a catch-all.
paymentMethod.title: paymentMethod

approvalStepState.description:
State of a single step within the approval chain. 

| State | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `approved` | This step was approved. |
| `current` | This step is the one awaiting a decision now. |
| `upcoming` | A later step, not yet reached. |
| `rejected` | This step was declined (stops the chain). |
approvalStepState.title: approvalStepState

approverType.description:
The role by which a person is entitled to approve a step. 

| Type | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `reportingManager` | The buyer's reporting manager. |
| `costCenterOwner` | The owner of the invoice's cost center. |
| `accountOwner` | The company's account owner. |
| `user` | A specific named user, assigned directly by an approval rule. |
approverType.title: approverType

supplierRef.description: Reference to the supplier (counterparty) of the invoice.

id.description: Supplier id. Fetch full supplier details from `GET /v1/suppliers/{id}`.

supplierRef.title: supplierRef

purchaseOrderRef.description: Reference to a purchase order the invoice is matched against (two/three-way match).
purchaseOrderRef.title: purchaseOrderRef

costCenterRef.description: Reference to a cost center (the internal unit that bears the cost).

id.description: Cost-center id. Use `GET /v1/cost-centers` to resolve full details.

costCenterRef.title: costCenterRef

expenseCategoryRef.description: Reference to an expense category — the customer's spend taxonomy (e.g. Software, Travel, Meals) used for accounting and analytics. Distinct from the cost center (which bears the cost) and from analytical fields (free custom dimensions).

id.description: Expense-category id. Use `GET /v1/expense-categories` to resolve full details.

expenseCategoryRef.title: expenseCategoryRef

buyerRef.description: The internal Spendesk member the invoice is assigned to — the "buyer", i.e. the person the spend is for and who is accountable for it. Distinct from the supplier (the external counterparty). This holds however the invoice was created: a member who submitted it, or the member an automatically-ingested invoice (shared mailbox, API) was assigned to. Name and email may be null for service accounts.
buyerRef.title: buyerRef

analyticalProperty.description: A value set for one analytical field. Analytical fields are the customer's own bookkeeping dimensions (custom fields) — e.g. project, team — used to classify and report spend. `valueId`/`valueName` are null when the field applies but no value is selected.
analyticalProperty.title: analyticalProperty

invoiceAnalyticalSplit.description: One allocation of the whole invoice to a cost center and/or analytical-field values, as a share of its total. Splits apply to the invoice as a whole, not to individual line items.

costCenter.description: Cost center this share is allocated to, or null when the split only sets analytical-field values.

percentage.description: Percentage of the invoice allocated to this split, from 0 to 100 (e.g. `25` means 25%). The splits of an invoice add up to 100.

analyticalProperties.description: Analytical-field values set on this split.

invoiceAnalyticalSplit.title: invoiceAnalyticalSplit

lineItem.description: A single line of the invoice, with its amounts and tax. Accounting coding is set on the whole invoice (see the invoice `costCenter`, `analyticalSplits` and `expenseCategories`), not per line.

unitPrice.description: Price per unit before tax, in `currency`'s smallest unit. Null when no net amount was captured, which can happen in any state (e.g. the single header-derived line of a credit note or of an older invoice whose net was never recorded).

netAmount.description: Line amount before tax (`quantity` x `unitPrice`), in `currency`'s smallest unit. Null when no net amount was captured, which can happen in any state (e.g. the single header-derived line of a credit note or of an older invoice whose net was never recorded).

taxAmount.description: Tax charged on this line, in `currency`'s smallest unit. Null when no net amount was captured, which can happen in any state (e.g. the single header-derived line of a credit note or of an older invoice whose net was never recorded), or when the gross amount is not known yet.

grossAmount.description: Line amount including tax (`netAmount` + `taxAmount`), in `currency`'s smallest unit. Null when the invoice has no gross amount yet (draft/incomplete).

costCenter.description: Always null: cost centers are set on the whole invoice, see the invoice `costCenter` and `analyticalSplits`.

expenseCategory.description: Always null: expense categories are set on the whole invoice, see the invoice `expenseCategories`.

analyticalProperties.description: Always empty: analytical-field values are set on the whole invoice, see the invoice `analyticalSplits`.

lineItem.title: lineItem

invoiceAttachment.description: A file supporting the invoice (documentary evidence). An invoice may have several.

mimeType.description: MIME type of the file (e.g. `application/pdf`, `application/xml` for e-invoices).

downloadUrl.description: Pre-signed URL to download the file, valid for at most 3 hours from when it was generated. Invoice responses are cached, so a re-fetch shortly after may return the same URL — download promptly and do not persist it.

invoiceAttachment.title: invoiceAttachment

invoiceDispute.description: Details of a dispute on the invoice (contested amount, duplicate, goods/services not received, quality issue…), overlaying whatever approval/payment state the invoice holds. Not populated yet: the invoice `dispute` field is always null for now, even on an invoice in dispute with the supplier (which reports `stage` `disputed`).

reasonCode.description: Machine-readable reason the invoice is disputed (e.g. a standard dispute-reason code). Not enumerated — treat as an opaque, extensible code. Null when only a free-text reason exists.

reason.description: Human-readable reason/comment for the dispute, if recorded.

invoiceDispute.title: invoiceDispute

paymentStatusReason.description: Why a payment failed or was returned. Present for those states; null otherwise.

code.description: Machine-readable reason/return code (e.g. an ACH return code like `R01`, or a bank rejection code). Opaque and extensible; null when only a message is available.

paymentStatusReason.title: paymentStatusReason

paymentFx.description: Currency conversion for this payment. Present only when the money actually moved in a currency different from the payment `currency`; null otherwise. The payment `amount`/`currency` are the invoice-side figures; these are the settlement side (what actually left the paying account).

settlementCurrency.description: Currency actually debited from the paying account.

settlementAmount.description: Amount actually moved, in `settlementCurrency`'s smallest unit.

rate.description: Exchange rate applied, such that `settlementAmount` is approximately `amount x rate` (units of `settlementCurrency` per one unit of the payment `currency`).

paymentFx.title: paymentFx

paymentFee.description: A fee incurred on the payment (deducted from the transfer or billed alongside it).

type.description: Kind of fee — `transfer` (bank/rail fee), `fx` (currency-conversion fee/spread), `intermediary` (correspondent-bank fee on international transfers), or `other`.

amount.description: Fee amount, in `currency`'s smallest unit.

paymentFee.title: paymentFee

payment.description: A single payment settling (or scheduled to settle) the invoice. An invoice may be settled by one or several payments — a Spendesk instalment plan, or one or more payments recorded as made outside Spendesk. `source` distinguishes the two. A failed/cancelled attempt and its retry appear as separate entries.

method.description: Means of payment, or null if not yet determined.

amount.description: Amount of this payment, in `currency`'s smallest unit. Settled (`paid`) payments in the invoice `currency` sum to the invoice `amountPaid`, except on credit notes, whose `amountPaid` is always 0 (null while `grossAmount` is unknown); a single payment may be a partial instalment.

currency.description: Currency this payment is made in — normally the invoice `currency`.

reference.description: Remittance reference sent with this payment so the supplier can reconcile it (often the supplier's payment reference or the invoice number). Null if none.

scheduledDate.description: Date the payment is scheduled to be executed. Null for externally-recorded payments that were never scheduled through Spendesk.

paidDate.description: Date the payment settled, or null if not yet settled.

statusReason.description: Why the payment failed or was returned; null for other states.

fx.description: Currency conversion applied; null when paid in the payment `currency`.

fees.description: Fees incurred on this payment (transfer, FX, intermediary…). Empty when none.

payment.title: payment

approver.description: A person entitled to act on an approval step.

userId.description: Member who nominally owns this approval slot (e.g. the reporting manager or cost-center owner). For `type: user` this is the directly-assigned approver.

actingUserId.description: Member acting on the nominal approver's behalf via a delegation. Null when the approval is not delegated (then the acting approver is `userId`).

isDelegated.description: Whether this approval is delegated (`actingUserId` differs from `userId`).

approver.title: approver

approvalDecision.description: Who acted on a step, when, and why. Null on a step until it has been acted on. The outcome (approved vs rejected) is given by the step's `state`.

byUserId.description: Member who took the decision (the acting approver, i.e. the delegate when delegated).

reason.description: Optional note left with the decision (e.g. a denial reason). Null when none.

approvalDecision.title: approvalDecision

approvalStep.description: One step in the approval chain. Steps are returned in execution order (the array index is the position); each must be approved for the invoice to advance to the next.

approvers.description: Members who may act on this step. Usually one; when several are listed, any one of them acting resolves the step.

decision.description: The decision recorded on this step, or null while it is `upcoming`/`current`.

approvalStep.title: approvalStep

approval.description: Detail of the approval workflow — the effective approval chain for this invoice's amount, with its completed, current and upcoming steps. The overall outcome shows in the invoice's `stage`; this object is the breakdown. Only the applicable chain is returned (amount-bracket internals are not exposed).

isAutoApproved.description: Whether the invoice was approved automatically by a rule rather than by approvers. When true, `steps` is empty.

autoApprovalReason.description: Why the invoice was auto-approved, or null when it was not.

steps.description: The approval steps in execution order. Empty when the invoice was auto-approved.

approval.title: approval

review.description: Finance/controller review that validates the invoice's data (amounts, coding, documentary evidence) for accounting. Distinct from `approval`, which authorises the spend — this checks the booking data. Null on the invoice when no review has been recorded.
review.title: review

invoice.description: Full representation of an invoice, returned by the detail endpoint. A superset of `invoiceSummary`, adding line items, the tax breakdown, currency conversion (FX), the payment history, the approval chain, accounting links, attachments and custom fields.

invoiceNumber.description: Supplier's invoice/credit-note number. Null if not captured.

exportStatus.description: Null until the invoice has an accounting payable (see `payableId`) — an invoice pending approval has nothing to export yet, which is distinct from `pending` (a payable exists but hasn't been exported).

dispute.description: Always null today, even if disputed (`stage` then shows `disputed`).

cancelledAt.description: When the invoice was cancelled/voided, or null if it is still active.

supplier.description: Null only on a draft (`stage` `pendingApproval`) with no supplier set yet.

purchaseOrders.description: Purchase orders this invoice is matched against (two/three-way match). Empty when the invoice references no PO. May hold several when one invoice consolidates multiple POs.

buyer.description: The internal member the invoice is assigned to (the buyer), or null.

costCenter.description: Cost center the invoice is coded to, or null when none is set. Set independently of `analyticalSplits`: the two are not reconciled and can disagree.

analyticalSplits.description: Allocation of the invoice total across cost centers and analytical-field values. Empty when the invoice is not split. Set independently of `costCenter`, so a split can name a different cost center.

expenseCategories.description: Expense categories the invoice is coded to, sorted by name. Empty when none is set. A split invoice can carry several, one per split. These ids are the ones the `expenseCategoryId` filter matches. Only the company's current expense-category field counts: if it is changed or removed, past invoices follow the new setting. A deleted category still shows on the invoices coded to it.

lineItems.description: The invoice's line items — always at least one. A non-itemised invoice is represented as a single line covering the whole amount. Lines carry no accounting coding (see `costCenter` and `analyticalSplits`); line `netAmount`/`taxAmount` sum to the header totals, except when the header total itself is null (draft/incomplete) while real captured line items exist.

netAmount.description: Total before tax, in `currency`'s smallest unit. Can be null in any state, not only draft/incomplete: always for credit notes, and for older invoices whose net amount was never recorded.

taxAmount.description: Total tax, in `currency`'s smallest unit, derived as `grossAmount - netAmount` (not summed from `lineItems`). For the tax-by-rate breakdown (VAT-return view), group the line items by `taxRate`. Null whenever `netAmount` or `grossAmount` is null, so in any state for credit notes and older invoices with no recorded net amount.

grossAmount.description: Total amount including tax (`netAmount` + `taxAmount`), in `currency`'s smallest unit. Positive for invoices (owed to the supplier); negative for credit notes (owed to the company). Null when the invoice has no gross amount yet (draft/incomplete).

amountPaid.description: Amount settled so far, in `currency`'s smallest unit: the sum of `payments` with status `paid` in the invoice `currency` (returned payments and payments in another currency are excluded). When `payments` is empty, it comes from the stored payment status instead: `grossAmount` if `paid`, otherwise 0 (even when `partiallyPaid`). Always 0 on credit notes, which have no stored payment status and never aggregate `payments`. When `grossAmount` is not known yet, it is null if it comes from the stored status (empty `payments`, or a credit note), but is still summed from `payments` when they are recorded.

amountDue.description: Outstanding balance still to be settled (`grossAmount` minus `amountPaid`), in `currency`'s smallest unit. Zero when fully paid. Null when `grossAmount` is not known yet (draft/incomplete).

currency.description: Null only on a draft (`stage` `pendingApproval`) with no currency set yet. Every amount on the invoice is then null too, because an amount can't be stated without its currency.

functionalAmount.description: `grossAmount` converted into the company entity's functional currency, in that currency's smallest unit. For accounting/reporting only — the supplier is paid `grossAmount` in `currency`, not this. Equal to `grossAmount` when the invoice is already in the functional currency. Null until the invoice has an accounting payable (see `payableId`) — this is not known before then, regardless of currency.

functionalCurrency.description: The company entity's functional currency — its primary currency for accounting and reporting. Equals `currency` when no conversion is needed. Null until the invoice has an accounting payable (see `payableId`).

functionalExchangeRate.description: Rate used to convert `currency` into `functionalCurrency`, applied as `functionalAmount` is approximately `grossAmount x functionalExchangeRate`. 1 when both currencies match. Null until the invoice has an accounting payable (see `payableId`).

issueDate.description: Date the supplier issued the invoice, as printed on the document (emission date). Null only on a draft (`stage` `pendingApproval`) with no issue date set yet.

dueDate.description: Date by which the invoice must be paid, per the supplier's payment terms. Null when no due date is known.

accountingDate.description: Posting date — the date the invoice is booked in the accounting ledger, which fixes the fiscal period it falls into. May differ from `issueDate`. Null until the invoice has an accounting payable (see `payableId`). Not the export date; see `exportedAt`.

payments.description: The payment history/plan. Empty until payments exist, and for older invoices not yet backfilled. `paymentStatus`, `amountPaid` and `amountDue` aggregate these entries, except when this array is empty, where they come from the stored payment status, and on credit notes, which have no stored payment status and always report `unpaid`.

review.description: Finance/controller review, or null if none has been recorded.

exportedAt.description: When the invoice was exported to the accounting system, or null if not exported.

documentaryEvidenceStatus.description: Null until the invoice has an accounting payable (see `payableId`) — there is nothing to attach evidence to yet for an invoice pending approval.

payableId.description: Id of the accounting payable this invoice produced, resolvable via the payables API. Null until the invoice has passed approval/controller validation and a payable has been created — not merely "not yet booked" in the accounting sense. One invoice maps to exactly one payable — line items and cost/analytical splits are allocations within that payable, not separate payables; a credit note is a separate document with its own payable.

attachments.description: Supporting files. Any without a download link is omitted, so may be partial.

createdAt.description: When the invoice record was created in Spendesk (ingest/submission time, not the issue date).

updatedAt.description: When any field on the invoice record last changed.

invoice.title: invoice

post.description:
**Allowed Scopes**: _`experimental:intake:write`_

Creates a presigned upload target for an intake file. This is step 1 of 3 in creating an intake from a document:

1. Create an upload with this endpoint to get a presigned URL and an `uploadId`.
2. Send the file to that URL, then poll [Get an intake file upload status](/reference/v2-get-intake-file-upload-status) until it returns a `documentId`.
3. Pass that `documentId` to [Create an intake](/reference/v2-post-company-intakes).

`contentLength` must be the exact byte size of the file you are about to send. The presigned policy pins that size, so an approximate value makes the upload in step 2 fail rather than this call.

To send the file, make a `multipart/form-data` request to `upload.url` using `upload.method`. Include every entry of `upload.fields` as a form field, then add the file itself as a field named `file`, last. The URL points to our storage provider and not to the Spendesk API, so do not send your access token with it. Upload before `upload.expiresAt`; once the URL has expired, call this endpoint again for a fresh one.

mimeType.description: Media type of the file. Allowed types: application/pdf, image/png, image/jpeg, application/xml, text/xml.

contentLength.description: Exact size of the file in bytes. The presigned upload rejects a file whose size differs from this value. Maximum: 10485760 (10 MB).

parameters.name: companyId
parameters.description: The company ID.

uploadId.description: Unique identifier for the file upload. Use it to poll the upload status once the file has been sent.

method.description: HTTP method to use when uploading the file.

url.description: Presigned URL where the file must be uploaded. It points to our storage provider rather than the Spendesk API, so send it no access token.

fields.description: Form fields that must all be sent with the file upload, as multipart/form-data. Send them first, then the file itself as a field named `file`.

expiresAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the presigned URL expires. Create a new upload once it has passed.

retry-after.description: Seconds to wait before retrying the request.

**Allowed Scopes**: _`experimental:intake:write`_

Returns the status of an intake file upload. This is step 2 of 3 in creating an intake from a document, after [Create an intake file upload](/reference/v2-create-intake-file-upload).

post.description:
**Allowed Scopes**: _`experimental:intake:write`_

Create a new incoming invoice or credit note for a company's invoice inbox. This is step 3 of 3 in creating an intake from a document.

`documentId` is required and comes from an earlier upload: create one with [Create an intake file upload](/reference/v2-create-intake-file-upload), send the file to the presigned URL, then poll [Get an intake file upload status](/reference/v2-get-intake-file-upload-status) until it reports `ready` and returns the `documentId`.

**Idempotent retries.** Send an optional `Idempotency-Key` header, any string of 1 to 255 characters such as your own system or ERP reference, to make a retry safe. Repeating a request with the same key for the same company returns `201` with the original intake and `alreadyExisted: true`, and creates nothing. The key is scoped to the company, so the same key sent by two companies creates two intakes, and it never expires. Once an intake is deleted, its key stays spent: retrying with it returns `409` rather than recreating the intake.

Note that **the request body is ignored when a key is reused**: if you send the same key with a different invoice, you receive the first intake back and the new body is discarded. Use a new key for each genuinely different invoice.

get.description:
**Allowed Scopes**: _`experimental:intake:read`_

Returns the company's intakes — supplier documents (invoices, credit notes, receipts) received by the company and being reviewed and processed — newest `createdAt` first, using forward-only cursor pagination: follow `meta.pagination.nextCursor` (or `nextUrl`) until `hasNextPage` is `false`.

Filter by `ids`, by lifecycle (`stage` for the coarse view, `status` for the fine-grained one), and by created, updated, issued or due date ranges. Filters combine with AND; `stage` and `status` intersect. Deleted intakes only appear when asked for: include `deleted` in `status`, or `processed` in `stage`, which covers it. A combination that cannot match anything, such as `stage=linked` with `status=received`, returns an empty page rather than an error.

The date filters come in two formats and are not interchangeable:

- `createdAfter`, `createdBefore`, `updatedAfter` and `updatedBefore` select on an instant, so they take a full ISO 8601 date-time such as `2026-08-01T09:30:00Z`.
- `issuedAfter`, `issuedBefore`, `dueAfter` and `dueBefore` select on a calendar date printed on the document, so they take `YYYY-MM-DD` such as `2026-08-01`, and include the whole of the day at each end.

Sending one form where the other is expected fails validation with a 400.

There is no filter on `type`. To list only invoices, or to leave receipts out, read `type` on each result and filter on your side.

Each result is a summary without the received files. [Get an intake](/reference/v2-get-company-intake) returns the same fields plus `documents`. Intake data is cached for up to 2 hours. Changes made through the API are returned by subsequent reads; changes made in Spendesk can take up to 2 hours to appear.

A 403 means either the token is not for `companyId`, or the Spendesk user the API key was created by is not a Controller, Administrator or Account Owner of that company.

fileName.description: Filename of the document, and the name it saves as when downloaded via `downloadUrl`. This is the original filename when one was captured at ingestion; otherwise a generated identifier with an extension derived from the mime type. Not guaranteed unique within this array.

mimeType.description: MIME type of the file (e.g. `application/pdf`, `application/xml` for e-invoices).

downloadUrl.description: Time-limited pre-signed URL to download the file. Expires at most 3 hours after the response is issued — download promptly and do not persist the URL (re-fetch the intake for a fresh one).

intakeDocument.title: intakeDocument

intakeLineItem.description: A single line of the invoice. Amounts are decimals in the intake's `currency`, not minor units, because they are transcribed as they appear on the document.

taxRate.description: Tax rate, as a percentage between 0 and 100.

intakeLineItem.title: intakeLineItem

intake.description: Full representation of an intake, returned by the detail endpoint. A superset of `intakeSummary`, adding the received documents and line items.

companyId.description: Id of the company entity that received the document.

source.description: How the document reached Spendesk, or null when not recorded.

supplier.description: The supplier that issued the document. Null when no supplier has been identified yet.

assigneeId.description: Id of the member the intake is assigned to — the person expected to complete and submit it. An id, not a name: resolve it with [Get Users](/reference/v1-get-users), which needs the `user:read` scope in addition to the intake read scope. Null while unassigned.

invoiceNumber.description: The supplier's invoice number as printed on the document. Null if not captured or the document is not an invoice.

creditNoteNumber.description: The supplier's credit-note number as printed on the document. Null if not captured or the document is not a credit note.

currency.description: Currency the document is denominated in. Null until captured, and also null when the captured value is not a three-letter code.

grossAmount.description: Total amount including tax, in `currency`'s smallest unit. Null until captured, and also null, even once captured, whenever `currency` is null or a code Spendesk does not support.

netAmount.description: Total amount before tax, in `currency`'s smallest unit. Null until captured, and also null, even once captured, whenever `currency` is null or a code Spendesk does not support.

netPayableAmount.description: Amount actually left to pay the supplier after deductions recorded on the document (e.g. an advance already paid, or an applied credit note), in `currency`'s smallest unit. Equals `grossAmount` when there are none. Only ever populated for intakes ingested through e-invoicing: it is always null for intakes created through this API and for intakes forwarded by email, where the null is permanent rather than capture-pending.

issueDate.description: Date the supplier issued the document, as printed on it (emission date). Null until captured.

dueDate.description: Date by which the document must be paid, per the supplier's payment terms. Null until captured or when no due date applies.

resultingDocument.description: The document the intake produced or was linked to. Null while the intake is in progress, and stays null for an intake that ends `refused` or `deleted` without producing one. Always null at `status: processed`, which records a controller clearing the to-process queue rather than a document being produced. A null can also mean the lookup failed rather than that none exists, on both List intakes and Get an intake.

Null whenever none is known, which is common even at `stage: processed` — that stage also holds refused and deleted intakes, which never produce one. On [List intakes](/reference/v2-list-company-intakes) a null is "unknown" rather than "none"; [Get an intake](/reference/v2-get-company-intake) is authoritative.

purchaseOrderId.description: Id of the purchase order the intake is matched against. Null when none.

correctsIntakeId.description: For a corrective document (e.g. a credit note cancelling or amending an earlier invoice): id of the intake it corrects. Null otherwise.

appUrl.description: Link to this intake in the Spendesk invoice inbox.

createdAt.description: When the intake was received by Spendesk (ingestion time, not `issueDate`).

updatedAt.description: When any field on the intake last changed. Null when never updated.

documents.description: Files received as part of the intake. Empty when no file is available. Download links are short-lived — see `downloadUrl`.

lineItems.description: Lines of the invoice, when any are held. Only the detail endpoint returns these — a full page of them would be too large.

lineItemsSource.description: How the line items were obtained. Null when none are held, or when they predate this field being recorded.

get.description:
**Allowed Scopes**: _`experimental:intake:read`_

Returns a single intake by id: everything [List intakes](/reference/v2-list-company-intakes) returns for it, plus the received files in `documents` — the invoice, credit note or receipt itself, and any companion file that arrived with it. This is the only endpoint that returns `documents`.

Each `downloadUrl` is pre-signed and expires at most 3 hours after the response was issued. Intake data is cached for up to 55 minutes, so a link you receive may already be part-way through those 3 hours. Download promptly, and fetch the intake again for a fresh link rather than storing one. Changes made through the API are returned by subsequent reads; changes made in Spendesk can take up to 55 minutes to appear.

A deleted intake is not a 404: it is still returned, with status `deleted`, and its documents can still be downloaded. A 404 means this company has no intake with that id. A 403 means either the token is not for `companyId`, or the Spendesk user the API key was created by is not a Controller, Administrator or Account Owner of that company.

get.description:
**Allowed Scopes**: _`experimental:card:read`_

Returns cards for the authenticated company. Lost, stolen, damaged, expired and cancelled cards are not listed.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Page size

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Filter by card type.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by card status label, case-sensitive: `Active`, `Blocked`, `New`, `Ready`, `Pre-activated`, `Hidden`, `Unknown` or `Aborted`. The legacy raw code (for example `ACT` or `BLO`) also matches. Lost, stolen, damaged, expired and cancelled cards are never listed, so filtering on those statuses returns no cards.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Filter by card owner user ID.

parameters.name: createdAfter
parameters.description: Return cards created on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC).

parameters.name: createdBefore
parameters.description: Return cards created on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC).

parameters.name: X-Company-Id
parameters.description: ID of the company the request acts on. Required with an organisation-level token; not needed with a company-level token.

200.description: Default Response

status.description: Card status label: `Active`, `Blocked`, `New`, `Ready`, `Pre-activated`, `Hidden`, `Unknown`, `Aborted`, `Lost`, `Stolen`, `Damaged`, `Expired` or `Cancelled`. A status code with no label is returned as the raw code, so treat unknown values as possible.

expiryDate.description: Expiry date printed on the card, set by the card provider. For multi-use cards this is NOT the date the card stops working — use multiUseCardExpiryDate instead.

multiUseCardExpiryDate.description: Expiration date of a multi-use card (ISO 8601 datetime): the end date chosen by the requester when the card was requested. Choosing an end date is mandatory when requesting a multi-use card, so this is set on every card of type multi_use; it is absent on all other card types. For multi-use cards it is the single source of truth for expiration — the date the card actually stops being usable — and always takes precedence over expiryDate.

availableBalance.description: What the card can spend right now, in `currency`, as a decimal in major units (12.5 means 12.50), not minor units.

spendingLimit.description: The card's monthly budget, in `currency`, as a decimal in major units (12.5 means 12.50), not minor units. Null when no monthly budget is set.

request.description: The originating request behind this virtual card: id, label, and the amount/currency the requester declared when creating it. amount and currency are in the requester's chosen (declared) currency, which may differ from the card's top-level currency and availableBalance — those are always in the company's currency. amount is a decimal in major units (12.5 means 12.50), not minor units. Null when the card has no linked request or when the request lookup failed — the two are not distinguished, and a failed lookup also nulls supplier and costCenter.

recurrence.description: Payment recurrence of the subscription, normally null for non-subscription cards. MONTHLY is also the fallback when the recurrence could not be resolved (no linked request, no interval on it, or a failed lookup), so it is not a confirmed cadence.

lastSuccessfulPaymentTime.description: Timestamp of the last settled card payment. Explicit null means confirmed: the card has never had one. The field being absent from the response instead means the lookup temporarily failed and the status is unknown — do not treat a missing field as null.

consideredAsLost.description: Computed at read time, not stored: true when receivedAt is null and the order was placed more than 30 days ago. receivedAt is not reliably recorded, so this is only a possible delivery-delay signal while the card is still Pre-activated; ignore it once the card is Active, Blocked or Ready. Not the card's own Lost status — never report the card as lost or the shipment as delayed from it; read the card's status for that.

cardOrder.description: Physical card order/shipping info: state, city/country (not the full address), trackingLink, dates, consideredAsLost, estimatedReceivedAt. Only populated for physical cards while pre-activated (status Pre-activated); null or absent otherwise — this does not mean the order info no longer exists after activation, see GET /v1/cards/:cardId/order for the status-independent lookup.

blockingReason.description: The single highest-priority reason this card is blocked — a card can hold several blocking reasons at once, so clearing this one may leave it blocked; do not present it as the only reason or as a complete unblocking instruction. Who/what has it blocked: user (a teammate — see userId/firstName/lastName), support (Spendesk support, identity never disclosed), controlRule (a company-configured spending control rule — could require a receipt, description, supplier, cost center, or custom fields depending on the company's rules; which rule and requirement is unmet is not exposed here), scheduledDeactivation (a recurring deactivation schedule configured for this physical card — reactivates automatically per that schedule), automatic (an automated process, no further detail exposed), or internal (an internal reason with no disclosable detail — contact the Spendesk support team for more information). Only populated while status is Blocked; null or absent otherwise. Use GET /v1/cards/:cardId/blocking-history for every reason on the card, active and past.

subscriptionBudget.description: The subscription's remaining budget as shown on the card in the product: budgetAmount (the declared budget), spentAmount (current billing period spend only, capped at budgetAmount), availableAmount (what is left of this period's budget; 0 when at or over budget), and spentPercent (rounded whole number 0–100; 100 can also mean just under budget). When the declared currency differs from the company's and the period's spend in the company currency, FX fees included, exceeds the budget, spentAmount, availableAmount and spentPercent are all 0, which means over budget, not unused. Use the card's transactions for actual spend. Amounts are in the subscription's own declared currency (the currency field here), which may differ from the card's top-level currency and availableBalance — those are always in the company's currency. All amounts are decimals in major units (12.5 means 12.50), not minor units. Only populated for subscription cards; null or absent otherwise.

retry-after.description: Seconds to wait before retrying the request.

200.description: Return a 2xx status to indicate that the data was received successfully

requestBody.description: Event linking to a payable that has been prepared (`eventType` is `prepared`). Use `/v1/payables/{id}` to get the full details.

200.description: Return a 2xx status to indicate that the data was received successfully

requestBody.description: Event linking to a newly created settlement. Use `/v1/settlements` to get the full details by filtering by id.

200.description: Return a 2xx status to indicate that the data was received successfully

post.description:
**Allowed Scopes**: _`experimental:webhooks:write`_

  Creates one or multiple webhook instances. Each instance will be linked to a company and a specific event.

  Maximum of 50 instances can be configured per company. 

  Be prepared to handle the same event multiple times. Clients should perform de-duplication on their side to avoid
   processing the same event multiple times.
  
  Spendesk will retry sending the event until it receives a 2xx response from the webhook endpoint.

  Upon failure the webhook instance will be retried immediately. If this retry fails second level retries will begin,
  followed by third level retries if necessary. 
  Finally if webhook instance is still failing the instance will be disabled. 

  - 1st level retry - ASAP.
  - 2nd level retry - every 10 minutes for 1 hour.
  - 3rd level retry - every 2 hours for 3 days.

  Spendesk will follow this retry policy on a best-effort basis but exact execution timestamps are not guaranteed. The 
  payload will include a unique `event.id` that can be used to deduplicate events. The `event.timestamp` will be the
  time the event published and can also be used to determine if an event has been processed before or is out of order.

  Events have lightweight payloads carrying the id of the resource in question. Events should be consumed in real-time
  by performing a corresponding GET on the resource in question, ensuring the most up-to-date data is used.
  
  Events will be published to the URL specified in the payload. If you need to allow-list incoming http requests from 
  Spendesk, you can find the list of IP addresses in "Using webhooks" guide.
    
  Events contain a signature in the header `x-spendesk-webhook-signature`. It is a HMAC SHA256 hash of the payload
  using the secret provided when creating the webhook instance. 
  This can be used to verify the authenticity of the event. When creating a webhook instance, the secret can be provided
  or a random one will be generated for you (it will be returned in the response only once). 
  If this secret needs to be changed, the webhook instance will need to be recreated to use the new secret. 
  We suggest using a secret of at least 32 characters long and recommend Spendesk generate this for you.
